notes: IMPORTANT: Despite its file name, this PDF is NOT the FRENIC-Mini C2 manual and NOT a datasheet for FRN0004C2S-4A. It is the FRENIC-Multi Instruction Manual INR-SI47-1094c-E (page_index 1: "Thank you for purchasing our FRENIC-Multi series of inverters." / "INR-SI47-1094c-E"); end page shows "2011-04 (D11c/C06)". Model types listed in it are FRN...E1S/E1E series (e.g. "FRN0.1E1S-2"); the string "C2S" does not appear anywhere in the extracted text. All parameters in this file therefore apply to FRENIC-Multi, not to the FRN0004C2S-4A drive.

The FRN0004C2S-4A model (nameplate photo vfd-manuals/Fuji/Fuji.jpeg: TYPE FRN0004C2S-4A, SOURCE 3PH 380-480V 50/60Hz, OUTPUT 3PH 380-480V 1-400Hz, 2.3kVA 3.1A, 150% 1min) is a FRENIC-Mini C2 model, covered by vfd-manuals/FRENIC/FRENIC-Mini-C2-instruction-manual.pdf (data/curated/fuji-frenic-mini-c2.json).

No Modbus register map or communication data addresses are tabulated in this manual; page_index 71 (printed 3-22) refers to "the RS-485 Communication User's Manual (MEH448b)" for input commands (function code S06). modbus_registers is therefore empty.

Default "*4" = varies by shipping destination (Table 5.1, page_index 96, printed 5-14: e.g. F03 Asia 60.0 / China 50.0 / EU 50.0 / Japan 60.0 / Taiwan and Korea 60.0). Default "*5" = varies by inverter capacity (Table 5.2, printed 5-15 and 5-16), not extracted.

Table text on these pages is laid out with names/ranges in separate text runs, so several evidence quotes contain only the code plus increment/unit/default columns; names, ranges and options were read from the rendered page images of the same pages. The extracted text contains split words (e.g. "T ime", "RT U", "proces sing") which are kept as-is in quotes.
setting_conditions holds the "Change when running" column as printed (Y, Y*, N).

v2 full extraction: parameters cover every code in Tables 5.1 (F, E, C, P, H, A, J, y codes); communication settings are y01-y20, y98, y99, H30; the manual has no register map (see RS-485 Communication User's Manual MEH448b) so modbus_registers is empty.
Specification tables for standard models (chapter 8.1) and Table 5.2 default values per capacity are graphics/not extractable; defaults marked *4/*5 point to Tables 5.1/5.2.
Alarm display codes appear in the text layer as printed (e.g. "0c1" for OC1, "0u1" for OU1).
Option lists for E01-E05/E98/E99 (input functions) and E20/E21/E27 (output functions) were reconstructed from the table text; labels for few multi-line entries were joined.

To squeeze out full performance of the braking resistor, configure data of function codes F50 and F51 while actually measuring the surface temperature of the braking resistor.

Check if the heat sink is not clogged. Clean the heat sink. (6) Replace the cooling fan. Visually check that the cooling fan rotates normally. Replace the cooling fan. knowledge_items.title: The motor does not rotate.
knowledge_items.description: The motor does not rotate.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) No power supplied to the inverter. (2) No forward/reverse operation command was inputted, or both the commands were inputted simultaneously (external signal operation). (3) No indication of rotation direction (keypad operation). (4) The inverter could not accept any run commands from the keypad since it was in Programming mode. (5) A run command with higher priority than the one attempted was active, and the run command was stopped. (6) The frequency command was set below the starting or stop frequency. (7) A frequency command with higher priority than the one attempted was active. (8) The upper and lower frequencies for the frequency limiters were set incorrectly. (9) The coast-to-stop command was effective. (10) Broken wire, incorrect connection or poor contact with the motor. (11) Overload Measure the output current. (12) Torque generated by the motor was insufficient. (13) Miss-/poor-connection of the DC reactor (DCR)
knowledge_items.remedy: (1) Turn ON a molded case circuit breaker (MCCB), a residual-current-operated protective device (RCD)/earth leakage circuit breaker (ELCB) (with overcurrent protection) or a magnetic contactor (MC). Check for voltage drop, phase loss, poor connections, or poor contacts, and fix them if necessary. (2) Input a run command. Set either the forward or reverse operation command to off if both commands are being inputted. Correct the assignment of commands FWD and REV to function codes E98 and E99. Connect the external circuit wires to control circuit terminals [FWD] and [REV] correctly. Make sure that the sink/source slide switch on the interface printed circuit board (interface PCB) is properly configured. (3) Input the rotation direction (F02 = 0), or select the keypad operation with which the rotation direction is fixed (F02 = 2 or 3). (4) Shift the operation mode to Running mode and enter a run command. (5) Correct any incorrect function code data settings (in H30, y98, etc.) or cancel the higher priority run command. (6) Set the value of the frequency command to the same or higher than that of the starting or stop frequency (F23 or F25). Reconsider the starting and stop frequencies (F23 and F25), and if necessary, change them to lower values. Inspect the frequency command, signal converters, switches, or relay contacts. Replace any ones that are faulty. Connect the external circuit wires correctly to terminals [13], [12], [11], and [C1]. (7) Correct any incorrect function code data settings (e.g. cancel the higher priority run command). (8) Change the settings of F15 and F16 to the correct ones. (9) Release the coast-to-stop command setting. (10) Repair the wires to the motor, or replace them. (11) Lighten the load (In winter, the load tends to increase.) Check that a mechanical brake is in effect. Release the mechanical brake, if any. (12) Increase the value of torque boost (F09 and A05) and try to run the motor. Check the data of function codes F04, F05, H50 through H53, A02, and A03. Change the V/f pattern to match the motor's characteristics. knowledge_items.cause: (1) The frequency command fluctuated. (2) The external frequency command device was used. (3) Frequency switching or multi-frequency command was enabled. (4) The connection between the inverter and the motor was too long. (5) The inverter output is hunting due to vibration caused by low stiffness of the load. Readjust the data of the output current fluctuation damping gain (H80 and A41). Check that the motor vibration is suppressed if you decrease the level of F26 (Motor sound (Carrier frequency)) or set F27 (Motor sound (Tone)) to "0." Decrease the carrier frequency (F26) or set the tone to "0" (F27 = 0).

knowledge_items.remedy: (1) Increase the carrier frequency (F26). Readjust the setting of F27 to appropriate value. (2) If it is over 40 q C, lower it by improving the ventilation. knowledge_items.description: Data of function codes cannot be changed
knowledge_items.cause: (1) An attempt was made to change function code data that cannot be changed when the inverter is running. (2) The data of the function codes is protected. (3) The WE-KP command ("Enable data change with keypad") is not input though it has been assigned to a digital input terminal. (4) The key was not pressed. (5) The setting data of function code F02, E01 through E05, E98, and E99 could not be changed.
knowledge_items.remedy: (1) Stop the motor then change the data of the function codes. (2) Change the setting of F00 from "1" or "3" to "0" or "2." (3) Input a WE-KP command through a digital input terminal. (4) Press the key after changing the function code data. (5) Turn OFF both FWD and REV .

causes.cause: An attempt was made to change function code data that cannot be changed when the inverter is running.
causes.check: Check if the inverter is running with Menu #3 "Drive Monitoring" using the keypad and then confirm whether the data of the function codes can be changed when the motor is running by referring to the function code tables.
remedy: Stop the motor then change the data of the function codes.

causes.cause: The data of the function codes is protected.
causes.check: Check the data of function code F00 (Data Protection).
remedy: Change the setting of F00 from "1" or "3" to "0" or "2."

causes.cause: The WE-KP command ("Enable data change with keypad") is not input though it has been assigned to a digital input terminal.
causes.check: Check the data of function codes E01, E02, E03, E04, E05, E98 and E99 and the input signals with Menu #4 "I/O Checking" using the keypad.
remedy: Input a WE-KP command through a digital input terminal.

causes.cause: The key was not pressed.
causes.check: Check whether you have pressed the key after changing the function code data.
remedy: Press the key after changing the function code data.

causes.cause: The setting data of function code F02, E01 through E05, E98, and E99 could not be changed.
causes.check: The inputs to the terminals of FWD and REV commands are concurrently turned ON.
remedy: Turn OFF both FWD and REV .

knowledge_items.title: – – – – (center bar) appears
knowledge_items.description: A center bar (– – – –) has appeared on the LED monitor.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Any of PID commands and their feedback related functions is disabled. (2) Connection to the keypad was in poor connection.
knowledge_items.remedy: (1) Set E43 to a value other than "10" or "12." Make sure that when you wish to view a PID command or a PID feedback amount, PID control is still in effect or J01 is not set to "0." Set J01 to "1: Enable (Process control normal operation)" or "2: Enable (Process control inverse operation)." (2) Replace the cable.

causes.cause: Any of PID commands and their feedback related functions is disabled.
causes.check: Make sure that when you wish to view other monitor items, E43 is not set to "10: PID command" or "12: PID feedback amount."
remedy: Set E43 to a value other than "10" or "12." Make sure that when you wish to view a PID command or a PID feedback amount, PID control is still in effect or J01 is not set to "0."
Set J01 to "1: Enable (Process control normal operation)" or "2: Enable (Process control inverse operation)."

causes.cause: Connection to the keypad was in poor connection.
causes.check: Prior to proceed, check that pressing the key does not take effect for the LED display. Check connectivity of the extension cable for the keypad used in remote operation.
remedy: Replace the cable.

knowledge_items.title: _ _ _ _ (under bar) appears
knowledge_items.description: An under bar ( _ _ _ _ ) appeared on the LED monitor when you pressed the key or entered a run forward command FWD or a run reverse command REV . The motor did not start.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) The voltage of the DC link bus was low.
knowledge_items.remedy: (1) Connect the inverter to a power supply that meets its input specifications.

causes.cause: The voltage of the DC link bus was low.
causes.check: Select 5_01 under Menu #5 "Maintenance Information" in Programming mode on the keypad, and check the voltage of the DC link bus, which should be: 200 VDC or below for three-phase 200 V, and 400 VDC or below for three-phase 400 V.
remedy: Connect the inverter to a power supply that meets its input specifications.

knowledge_items.title: appears
knowledge_items.description: Parentheses ( ) has appeared on the LED monitor while the keypad displaying the Drive Monitor.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) The data to be displayed could not fit the LED monitor (e.g. overflown).
knowledge_items.remedy: (1) Adjust the setting of E50.

causes.cause: The data to be displayed could not fit the LED monitor (e.g. overflown).
causes.check: Check that the product of the output frequency and the display coefficient (E50) does not exceed 9999.
remedy: Adjust the setting of E50.
